messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT - SEV2: elevated incorrect KV reads detected from prefix-cached path in us-west-2. Error signature: `kv_read_mismatch`. Rolling count spike at 1835002450. Paging on-call.
oliver: i’m on pager, joining.
sara: joining as backup SRE. any customer hits yet?
incident-bot: 3 tenants flagged: acme-fin, beta-payments, metrics-svc. ~0.8% of total requests experienced stale/mismatched values. No data loss reported, but correctness impact.
mike: quick triage: is this a cache eviction bug or stale prefix aggregation? any recent deploys to prefix cache? 
oncall-ml: there was a quantized runtime tweak rolled 3h ago that touches KV fetch path but not supposed to affect semantics. instrumenting now.
eva: grabbing logs for affected keys. sample: `{key: "user:acct:1234", backend_val: "v10", cached_val: "v9"}`
chris: can we temporarily disable prefix aggregation cache for reads to see if miscompare drops?
oliver: yes. mitigation plan suggestion: 1) enable KV bypass for read correctness on affected shards 2) apply per-tenant read QPS caps for the 3 tenants 3) route 25% of traffic to non-cached fallback pool for canary 4) notify customers and oncall handoff.
sara: +1. prefer to do a quick canary (25%) first before global disable.
mike: agree. execute canary then scale if green.
oliver: running command to set flag on shard group us-west-2-a: 
``` 
POST /api/v1/runtime-flags
{ "flag": "kv_prefix_cache_enabled", "value": false, "scope": "shard:us-west-2-a", "reason": "inc-1835002468-temp-bypass" }
```
(oncall-ml) deployed, got 200.
eva: monitoring metrics... mismatch rate dropped ~70% within 90s on canary pool.
chris: good. roll to remaining shards in region after 5m observation window.
incident-bot: ACTION: set per-tenant read caps: acme-fin=60qps, beta-payments=40qps, metrics-svc=30qps. Applying now.
oliver: applying rate caps via quota service: `quotactl set acme-fin read 60 --reason inc-1835002468` done.
mike: also enabling traffic shaping at edge to divert 25% to fallback pool: `edgectl route set --service kv-read --fallback-pool fallback-noncached --weight 25%`
eva: logs show fallback reads returning correct backend values; no errors.
sara: customer impact note: acme-fin and beta-payments report increased latency (~120-200ms extra) from fallback path, but correctness restored. metrics-svc had occasional 5xxs before; those have stopped.
mike: good. status update for customers: "We detected inconsistent KV reads for a small subset of tenants. We have enabled a temporary correctness bypass and applied per-tenant throttles while we investigate. No data loss. Working on a permanent fix." draft posted to status page.
chris: can we revert the quantized runtime tweak in prod? i'd rather roll that back from canary then promote after fix.
oncall-ml: rollback queued for canary group. executing now.
incident-bot: DEPLOY BOT: rollback/quant-tweak -> success on canary, pending region-wide.
eva: anomaly rate trending down region-wide after disabling prefix cache and rollback.
oliver: next steps: 1) keep kv_prefix_cache disabled for us-west-2 for 2 hours 2) run binary search on prefix aggregation code path to reproduce 3) schedule a hotfix for semantics bug 4) create postmortem owner mike.
mike: grabbing postmortem. I'll own and loop in runtime team. setting INC ticket INC-2026-142.
sara: planning handoff to daytime oncall in 30m. @oncall-ml you’re on for investigations after handoff.
oncall-ml: acknowledged, i'll take after handoff.
mike: reminder: notify top 10 customers via account reps; include workaround (temporary consistency bypass) and ETA for fix ~24-48h.
chris: adding observability follow-ups: add histogram on `kv_read_mismatch_by_prefix` and an alert at 0.1% sustained.
oliver: doc update: added runbook steps under "incidents/kv-consistency". link: https://confluence.internal/infra/kv-consistency
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, correctness restored for majority, customer-facing note posted. severity downgraded to SEV3. Keep thread for postmortem and final resolution.
sara: handing off to daytime now. oncall-ml will own remaining actions. I'll stay on call if anything regresses.
oncall-ml: taking ownership. will keep monitoring and update this thread. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
mike: postmortem owner will draft timeline and RCA. target doc in 48h.
chris: closing immediate action items. leaving alert rules to runtime team.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (mitigation active) at 1835003120. Follow-up: postmortem required.
